## Rigid Body Instances

### What it does
This graph demonstrates basic rigid body instancing. 

### Inputs and outputs
This graph is self-contained, the instances are simple primitives, the ground plane, bowl and agitator are simple extrusions and volume to mesh.
The graph outputs MToA renderable objects.

### How it works
This graph is demonstrating rigid body instances.  This is a method where the rigid bodies are instances driven by points.  This makes is faster than polygon based rigid bodies.  The instance points and instance geometry are created - the points from a cylinder and the instances are basic primitives in this example.  The rigid bodies are then simulated.

_notes.text: Because a torus has a hole in it, a convex hull will produce a collision shape without a hole in it.  Here we are using *convex_hull* in the *method* parameter - while this speeds up the simulation, it is less accurate.  Change the *method* property to *convex_decomposition* to see the difference.
running the *frame* property from the ***time*** compound through an ***evaluate_fCurve*** allows animation of the object.
Higher poly-count, better looking render.  The collision object is much much simpler, for speed.
Comparing the vector between a point on the surface and the surface normal at that point.  If the sign of the dot product is negative, the point is **inside** the object.
